assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine, general operation. It is among the most-used bond-forming reactions in medicinal and process chemistry, with ligand design as a clear conceptual advance. Exactly the kind of general method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination and the ligand classes that made it broadly useful. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling (and Migita's related work) was a precursor but required stoichiometric tin reagents; I would not include him. Hartwig also appears in the C-H functionalization entry, so a single prize cannot comfortably honour him twice.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use, mechanistic study and industrial scale-up. Interpretation is stable and recognition is overdue rather than premature. The 2010 cross-coupling prize is a precedent that must be weighed; its scope explicitly did not include C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Relative credit between early tin-amide work and the catalytic general method; my recollection of the history is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were impractical before. Widely adopted in discovery chemistry and increasingly in process settings; a real conceptual shift for synthetic planning.
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson reported the foundational synthetic applications around 2008, with Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi also credited. A three-person set from the listed names is defensible, but the allocation is contestable. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: About 15 to 18 years of rapid, independent adoption; the field is large and robust, though still evolving, and some claims about mechanism and scalability are debated.
uncertainties: MacMillan's earlier prize and the risk of seeming repetitive.
Multiple near-simultaneous contributors, including those with earlier inorganic photochemistry precedent.
Whether practical scalability matches the academic impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective catalytic functionalization of otherwise inert C-H bonds changes retrosynthetic logic, shortening syntheses and enabling late-stage modification. Directing-group and ligand-controlled strategies have now spread broadly through academic and pharmaceutical practice.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand- and template-enabled selectivity), Hartwig (borylation and related) and Sanford (Pd/high-valent mechanism and scope) are leading, distinct contributors; Daugulis and Smith also made key early observations. A fair three-person split is possible but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Substantial and growing industrial adoption, though full generality and routine step-economy at scale are still maturing. Somewhat earlier than C-N coupling but strong.
uncertainties: Selectivity remains substrate-dependent and some methods need directing groups.
Allocation across Yu, Hartwig, Sanford, Daugulis and Smith is contentious; Hartwig overlap with B065.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts. N-heterocyclic carbenes underlie modern metathesis and cross-coupling catalysts, and main-group chemistry more broadly. The discovery was conceptually surprising and has proven durable.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 isolable imidazol-2-ylidene is the landmark; Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene (1988) is the other decisive precedent. Nolan, Rovis and Bode drove applications, but I regard the core discovery as a two-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation and wide practical use. Timing is mature, if not pressing.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's 1988 push-pull carbene and Arduengo's 1991 stable NHC.
Whether the application side (catalysis) should be credited rather than the isolation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical, a real extension of synthetic methodology to molecules of biological size. It is chemically clear and has had lasting use in protein science.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported native chemical ligation in 1994; Muir contributed expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky's desulfurization-based extensions are significant but later. A three-person prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use; confirmed, though routine use remains specialist and some applications have been overtaken by recombinant methods.
uncertainties: How broadly the method is used outside specialist labs.
Allocation among Kent, Dawson, Muir and Danishefsky.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly produces discrete, well-defined cages and capsules from simple components, with host-guest chemistry and confined catalysis. Conceptually elegant and chemically original, though its practical reach beyond supramolecular chemistry is more limited.
assessment.attribution: Fujita, Raymond and Stang are the founding contributors of coordination-driven discrete assemblies, with Nitschke and Ward as later developers. A three-person set is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent work; mature. Supramolecular chemistry was honoured in 1987 and 2016, so the field has recent precedent.
uncertainties: Real-world adoption and application impact are modest.
Distinction between Fujita's and Stang's overlapping contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced protein degradation by bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological modality that reframes how small molecules engage targets. The molecule design logic is chemical and has real consequences for drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies reported the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli advanced the structure-guided VHL-based design. Handa and Ito's work on thalidomide-cereblon is an essential parallel part, and the allocation is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging; independent confirmation of mechanism is solid but the long-term impact is not yet settled, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Complex credit allocation including the thalidomide-cereblon discovery.
Borderline between medicinal and basic chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermolecular oxidative addition of unreactive alkane C-H bonds to a metal centre was a landmark organometallic observation that reshaped thinking about alkane activation. It underpins later C-H functionalization concepts.
assessment.attribution: Bergman's 1982 iridium work is the singular discovery as credited, with Graham's parallel report not in the supplied credit; a single-laureate prize would be simple, though it may seem incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and conceptually influential, but direct practical application is limited, and later C-H functionalization (B043) has taken its practical impact forward.
uncertainties: Contemporaneous work by W. A. G. Graham is not credited in this entry.
Whether fundamental organometallic significance is enough without broad practical impact.
